valuation.method: Bank: forward P/E on FY2027 (year to Oct 2027) EPS, viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), computed in CAD and converted once to USD. Ratio: 1 NYSE RY share = 1 common share (ratio 1:1), with no depositary receipt. The 40-F cover page (FY2024 filing, form40_24.pdf) lists Common Shares, symbol RY, on the New York Stock Exchange, and the filing says the common shares are listed on the TSX and NYSE. This contradicts the task's ADR label; the listing is the common share itself, so no ADR conversion applies. FX: USD/CAD 1.4257 CAD per USD, Bank of Canada daily rate for 2026-11-13 (Valet FXUSDCAD), held constant to the target date. Earnings base: nine-month FY2026 adjusted EPS C$12.26 plus a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate of C$4.28 gives about C$16.54 for FY2026; base FY2027 EPS C$17.90 is +8% on that. Cross-check (not an input): Barchart FY2027 C$17.41 and Benzinga US$12.81 (about C$18.26 at 1.4257). Base: C$17.90 x 16x = C$286.4 = US$200.88. Bear: C$16.50 x 14x = C$231.0 = US$162.03. Bull: C$18.90 x 18x = C$340.2 = US$238.62. A P/E basis is used rather than P/TBV because goodwill and intangibles were not sourced; book check: common equity C$133,922m / 1,384,554k shares = C$96.73 per share, so the close (C$288.43) is about 3.0x book, consistent with an approximately 18% ROE. Dividend: C$1.76 declared for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, C$7.04 a year = US$4.94 at the same FX.

bear.driver: Credit losses rise and NII growth stalls, so FY2027 EPS is flat on FY2026 (about C$16.50) and RBC trades at a discount multiple of 14x as capital return slows.

base.driver: FY2027 EPS of C$17.90 (+8% on the FY2026 run-rate, within the cross-check consensus range) with ROE near 18% and CET1 around 13.5%, at a 16x multiple close to today's.

bull.driver: Capital markets and fee growth plus lower capital drag push EPS to C$18.90 and the multiple to 18x as ROE holds above 18%.

valuation.implied_by_close: The close of US$202.31 equals C$288.43 at 1.4257, which is 16.1x base EPS of C$17.90 and 16.6x the C$17.41 consensus low. The simple mean of the five named targets (US$208.29, about C$297) is 16.6x base EPS, about 4% above the base target; the gap is an EPS-or-multiple difference, and the analysts' assumptions are not sourced.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E on base EPS moves the base target by US$12.56 (6.2 pp of the close). A C$1.00 change in FY2027 EPS moves it by US$11.2 at 16x (5.5 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Quarterly adjusted EPS against the C$4.28 Q3 run-rate and adjusted ROE (18.1% in Q3 FY2026). The base case needs about C$4.48 per quarter across FY2027 with CET1 held near 13.5%.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year FY2026 results, 2026-12-03 08:30 ET (aggregate earnings timestamp).

analyst_notes: Six named analysts were sourced with dated calls from May 19 to Sep 3, 2026, and the sample is partial. The post-Q3 moves are CIBC cut US$217 to US$210 (Hold), KBW raised US$221 to US$226 (Hold, reiterated), Jefferies US$187 to US$189 (Hold), and Scotiabank US$217 to US$218 (Buy); the one- and two-dollar moves may be FX rounding rather than revisions. Named targets average US$208.29, about 4% above the US$200.88 base case, but no sampled firm documents a 12-month horizon, so none enter the weighted target. Excluded: Raymond James (Hold, US$214 to US$208) is dated Nov 17, after the reference close; Desjardins (Buy, US$224 to US$221, Nov 12) and National Bank (Buy, US$222 to US$224, Aug 30) are firm-only with no named analyst. The Q3 release time is not verified, so earnings_at uses end of day on Aug 27.
